Who are said to be taken away as maidservants and placed in the king’s service, 198. Under the name of maidservants the affections of the soul may be understood, ibid.

The sublimity of angels is understood under the name of a mirror, 8. Angels are believed to have been sanctified in the Son, 44. Angels can no longer fall, 58. The holy angels, conscious of their weakness, have been strengthened by God, ibid. By the merit of humility they rose into the glory of love, ibid. The holy angels in blessed eternity are intoxicated with the wine of wisdom, 417.

Angels are girded with humility before they are sent for ministry, 59. They are sent to gather those for whose salvation they are daily sent, 60. The fellowship of brotherhood between two rational creatures, 411. Through the hollow of the wall the very protection of angelic guardianship is figured, 420. After the Incarnation angels do not permit themselves to be worshiped by human beings, 454.

An angel fell through presumption of his own virtue, 58. In the fallen angels let man learn what he should fear, ibid. Reprobate angels are expressed by the name Philistines, 125, 165. Through the sin of pride they lost the state of eternal life, 125, 165, 287. Why the first of the angels fell through pride, 179.

Reprobate angels can never repent of the pride they committed, 149. If God spared neither golden vessels, what will happen to one of bronze? 58. Reprobate angels do not recover love of the blessedness they lost, 149. The losses of the angels are to be repaired in heaven through elect human beings, 172.

To tighten means the same as to constrict, 36.

The anguish in which those are found who are constricted after being caught in the snare of an evil habit, 348.

To fashion the likenesses of tumors (*ani*) means to recall with a repentant heart the shamefulness of one’s recently sinning limbs, 147. Why the likeness of a tumor is made of gold, ibid. These likenesses are made by remembering and gilded by weeping, ibid. Five tumors are commanded to be made because satisfaction by all the Gentiles is enjoined, 147. Five tumors are commanded to be made so that compunction may arise from all the senses, ibid. The likenesses of the tumors are made for shame, so that we may be confounded by the stains of our foulness, ibid. They are gilded for security, ibid. What is signified by each of the Philistine cities returning one tumor and one mouse, 159.

The soul of the elect is the temple of God, 114.

The she-asses of Kish are sinful souls, 203. They are lost because through impurity they have been separated from Christ’s service, ibid.

The souls of the perfect are brides, 212. Souls beginning a new pursuit of life are called young women, 402. The holy soul is compared with a dove, 415. The soul becomes a friend through faith, a dove through simplicity, and beautiful through action, 419. Chaste souls are lilies in which Christ delights, 421. The holy soul is a locked garden, 432. Why it is compared with a sealed spring, 433. Why with palm trees, 452. The holy soul is called dawn, moon, and sun, 447. Holy souls are called queens, 444. The soul is endowed with three natures, 467. From the soul come rationality and sensuality; through the former we agree with angels, through the latter with beasts, 349. Whatever can be explained concerning the whole Church can also be explained concerning any soul, 403.

What it means to pour out the soul in the Lord’s presence, 20. The condition of the soul enjoying sublime light, 33. The exultation of the soul that has experienced the force of love in the Bridegroom’s chamber, 54. The soul exulting in every victory over the passions asserts its heart—that is, the freedom of its mind, [Col. 1428] ibid. What it means to carry one’s soul in one’s hands, 54. For the soul, to ask is to desire, and to rejoice is to sing, 57. Why God withdraws the sweetness of His presence from the soul, 104. God’s intimacy with the holy soul, ibid. The love and joy of souls hearing God call them, ibid. To desire always to hear God’s ineffably sweet speech, ibid. When God speaks, the mind is lifted up from the darkness of its corruption, ibid. When God is silent through the withdrawal of grace, it is subjected to the same darkness, ibid. The rest of the chosen soul is not only its own delight but also the Bridegroom’s, 213. All souls clinging to God are Solomon’s skins, 409. The devout soul ought to imitate the love and lament of the turtledove, 414. The soul’s little bed is a refuge and secret place from all disturbances, 422. The sighs of the soul languishing with love are directed to the saints as intercessors, 439. From this exile the faithful soul ascends to heaven, supported upon Christ, 455. The soul troubled by grief over sin, 469. Just as harsh things wound the flesh, so soft things kill the soul, 490. The interior and exterior enemies of the faithful soul, 490. The holy soul desiring God alone perfectly prays for this one thing: that God never depart from it even for an hour, 493. What the food of the elect soul is, 38, 67, 206, 218. The elect soul sees the day of eternity dawning upon it in death because it did not behold the darkness of this life, 321. The threefold condition of the soul: in grace, in rest, and in glory, 56. For the elect soul to ask for these things in the song is to desire such great gifts, 57. A soul divided from God cannot perceive God, 471. What the death of the soul is and what its effects are, 548. What a menstruating soul is, 514. What a Christian soul ought to do, 555.

The blindness of carnal people who seek the care of souls, 177. The greedy consider their soul inferior to every object they are able to desire, 191. Whoever is placed over the care of souls should pursue a harsh life, 338. Those suitable for the care of souls must be sought with tireless labor, 381. What the care of souls produces among faithful preachers, 163. Whoever seeks the profit of souls does everything spiritually, 203. The Shepherd of souls ought not to devote himself to the leisure of a secluded life, 335. See *Pastor*, *Rector*, *Prelate*.

Why the holy animals are described as having eyes all around, 385.

Anna, the wife of Elkanah, figures the Church, 10, 41, 65. What Anna’s barrenness signifies, 10, 32. What the ten sons signify, than whom Anna’s husband is better to her, 15. What Anna speaking in her heart represents, 18. What the movement of her lips signifies, ibid. Why Anna is said to rise early with her husband, 22. What Anna offering the child not alone but with her husband signifies, 28. Anna patiently endured the injury done to her by Eli and appeased and honored the priest by the humility of her reply, 37. Why Anna is described as weeping copiously before her vow, 38. Anna first wept with a bitter spirit and thus was able to weep copiously, ibid. What is signified by Anna conceiving after the cycle of days, 39. Anna, barren, wept; in giving birth, she exulted, 41. Anna’s horn is the power of the Church, ibid. What is figured by the mother bringing a small tunic for her little son, 83. What the sons and daughters whom Anna bears signify, ibid. What Anna’s asking the Lord for a male child signifies, [Col. 1429] 16. What Anna, thought to be drunk, denotes, 18. What it signifies for Anna to be afflicted, 36. Anna possessed the spirit of prophecy, 41.

The tabernacle of Antichrist is the love of treachery by which he contradicts the Redeemer’s faith, 45. The martyrs who will suffer under Antichrist, 444.

We enter caves and cisterns when we guard our sense of smell from the world’s obscenities and our ears from hearing empty talk, 286.

Bees, making honey, gather it from various flowers, 232. The flowers of eternal fruits are the works of the saints, ibid.

Although the conversion of apostates is extremely difficult, it is nevertheless not impossible, 312. Who these apostates are, ibid.

The apostles, when weak and when strong, clothed with power from on high, 47, 503. First the bow of the strong must be overcome, and afterward the weak must be girded with strength, 48. The apostles are called princes, 51. Who is the poor man who sits with princes, ibid. Under the name of heavens the apostles are signified, 53, 503, 532. The remarkable holiness of the apostolic company, 75. The peoples marveled at the apostles, transformed by the Spirit rushing upon them, 249. Their heavenly origin was unknown, ibid. The apostles are the Bridegroom’s breasts, 408. The apostles abandoned obstinate Jews and passed over to preach to the Gentiles, 410. The apostles’ struggles against those whom they called to the faith, ibid. The apostles are called the children of their mother Jerusalem, ibid. The apostles were instructed in faith by Christ’s miracles and strengthened for suffering, 442. The apostles are signified by Christ’s legs, ibid. They are called marble columns, ibid. Upon what bases those columns rest, ibid. Why those bases are called golden, ibid. The vineyard was assigned to the apostles and cultivated by them, 460. The apostles are called Christ’s feet, 490. The power of the heavens comes from the Holy Spirit: the apostles, from being weak, became strong, 503. While the apostles doubted, women stood firm during Christ’s Passion, 514. The apostles are called the stones of the Church, 523. The apostles proclaiming peace, ibid. Why their feet are beautiful, ibid. The apostles had pity on the earth, that is, on the Jews, 524. Through fishermen Christ subdued kings, ibid., 529. The earth obtained fertility through the rains of apostolic preaching, 532. Who are called the works of God’s hands, namely the apostles, ibid. Who are called the works of God’s fingers, ibid. All the faithful are the children of the apostles, 534. The apostles are called servants because of the labor of their work, and sons because of the transformation of newness, 535.

What it means to appear continually in the Lord’s presence, 24. The Lord appears in various ways, 111. The word of God must be understood before He Himself appears to us, ibid. Those to whom God appears possess true speech, not the speech of heretics, 112. The word of the Lord is found in the addition of appearance, 124.

What drawing water signifies, 166, 209. Many waters signify great tribulations, 457. With what waters sins are washed, 495. To draw divided waters from the eyes means to mourn sins individually, 513. Land without water is a soul without grace, 550.

The unclean spirit is signified by the north, 434.

Who the mystical cultivators of fields are, 183, 193. What it means to plow with an ox and an ass, 262.

A pastor should not follow his own judgment, 227. Since free will was impaired in the first parent, we cannot will what is good unless aided by grace, 550. In victory over temptations, what belongs to the gift of grace and what to free will, 170.

The fruitless tree handed over to fire, 31. What the good tree bearing good fruits is, 198. We cut off branches for ourselves by imitating the examples of better people, 296. Wild trees signify the rest of humanity; Christ is figured by the apple, 416.

What the Ark represents, 27. What it means to sleep in the place where the Ark of God is, 99. What it means to bring the Ark of God from Shiloh into the camp, 127. What it means for the Ark to have come into the Hebrew camp, 128. What the Ark of God captured by the Philistines signifies, 130. Who captures the Ark of God, ibid. When the Ark is captured, Eli’s two sons die, 131. What it means for the city to howl at the capture of the Ark, 132. What Eli’s falling from his seat and dying after learning of the Ark’s capture signifies mystically, 134. The Ark is captured—that is, the sacraments of Scripture are retained by the understanding of true believers, 136. Israel’s glory did not perish but was transferred to the Church, ibid. The Ark of God was brought into idol temples when the faith was implanted in the minds of the Gentiles, 137. What the Ark placed beside Dagon represents, ibid. The Ark carried around among the Philistines signified the Gospel to be preached and carried among the Gentiles, 140. The Ark of God remains among those who embrace the true faith with love, ibid. The Ark carried around figures the sacraments of faith taken from some and revealed to others, 141. What the proper place of the Ark is, ibid. The Ark is sent back to its place when a small knowledge of Scripture is completed through the passage of the present life, 144. When we shall see the glory of God’s Ark displayed in its own place, ibid. The empty Ark is divine knowledge without good works, ibid. The empty Ark is sent back when the mind of one coming to the faith does not take pains in good works, ibid. The empty Ark is not sent away if what is owed to it is rendered for sin, 145. The affliction of devout repentance is owed to the Ark for sin, ibid. What debt to the Ark is paid, ibid. The debt owed to the Ark for sin is properly paid if likenesses of tumors and mice are made of gold, 146. Why the Ark, when it is to be brought back, is commanded to be placed upon a new cart, 150. The Ark is held so that it may be placed upon the cart; once placed upon it, it is released to go, 151. Why the released Ark is said not to go but to ascend, 152. The Bethsamites who presumed to look upon the Ark were struck down, 160. To whom the Ark of God should be entrusted, 161. The Ark signifies the spiritual knowledge of Holy Scripture, 162. The priest possesses the Ark when he does not have a mind empty of spiritual knowledge, 311. What Saul’s commanding Ahijah to bring the Ark near signifies, ibid. What Saul’s commanding the Ark to be brought near and then ordering the priest to draw back his hand denotes, ibid.

What the bow of the strong is, 47, 58. Which bow of the strong has been overcome, ibid.

The sand of the sea signifies the multitude of enemies, that is, of evil spirits, 283.

What the little beds of spices planted by perfumers represent, 441.

The name of silver designates divine utterances, 206, 426. Silver in the child’s hand is the divine word in the power of knowing, ibid. Under the name of silver sacred preaching is signified, 414. By silver every earthly substance is understood, 460.

To rebuke is more than to correct, 468.

By the ram the strength of one’s own innocence is expressed, 320. What it means for Saul to have spared the rams of Amalek, 351.

Why the disobedient are like diviners, 361. From where diviners get their name, 362. What kind of sin divination is, ibid.

The ancient weapons of the devil are gluttony and elation, 6. The weapons that were previously weapons of iniquity are to become weapons of justice, 147. Who are the armorers and makers of the tyrants’ chariots, 183. To forge weapons is to gather in a reprobate mind various means of doing harm, ibid. What weapons are to be forged against the enemy, 194. The weapons supplied to us for spiritual warfare are not human inventions but the divine writings, 295. What is signified by the armor-bearer carrying weapons with which another fights, 298. What is represented by the armor of the strong hanging from David’s tower, 429.

What it means to eat the shoulder placed before one, 224. What part of the shoulder is deliberately preserved, ibid. In the shoulder of the breast the strength of action is signified, 223.

What it means to buy spices, 336. Spices signify the gifts of the Holy Spirit, 403. They also designate holy virtues, ibid.

It belongs to the arrogant to speak lofty things while boasting, 57.

The liberal arts should be learned so that the divine utterances may be understood more subtly, 295.

When judging an artisan’s skill, one should look to his completed work, not to what has merely been begun, 209.

What it means for Christ to ascend from His own city, 10. Little ones should not presume to ascend, 25. How we ascend on appointed days, 32. Which days are called ascents, 33. The Ephraimite man, by ascending from his city, reproves our negligence, ibid. Whoever watches prepared for the ascent of the appointed days is made worthy to be visited more frequently by divine favor, ibid. Which are the days of ascent on which we have determined to adore and sacrifice, 35. To ascend by the merits of the virtues is to advance daily toward better things, 152. What it means for the Lord to ascend from us, 160. What it means for evil spirits to ascend, 167, 284. What it means to ascend on high, 217. What it means for a pastor to ascend, 290. For the reprobate, to ascend means to progress from evil to worse, 373. For the proud, to ascend into his house means to exalt himself up to the measure at which he is to be condemned, ibid. By how many and what steps one must ascend to heaven, 536. What ascents are to be arranged in the heart of the blessed man, 536.

The asses of the elect are those upon whom the burdens of obedience are imposed, 185. The asses figure the wanton movements of the soul, 198. Which asses are placed in the king’s service, ibid. The she-asses of Kish are sinful souls, 203. Why Christ, going toward His Passion, sat upon an untied she-ass and its colt, ibid. What the she-asses whom Samuel tells Saul have been found signify, 221. What the men of Saul saying that the she-asses have been found represent, 231. Our father Christ, having dismissed the she-asses, is concerned for us, 232. The ass signifies carnal love, 262, 344. See *Amalek*.

A subordinate is taken up when through the teacher’s word he is elevated into knowledge of heavenly things, 222.

The morning assumption is the resurrection accomplished by God in the morning, 541.

Most hearers, receiving the words of preaching, are pierced even to tears and quickly return to iniquity, 65. What it means to hear God, 120, 273. A preacher accomplishes nothing by exhorting if the hearer does not direct his mind toward what is said, 271. Those who despise the admonitions of preachers try to gnaw at their lives with a slanderous tooth, 303. The heart of the chosen hearer is the altar of God, 377. To hear obediently is to carry out in obedience what is commanded by one’s superiors, 380. To go out to meet a preacher is to hear willingly the word he preaches, 388. To be sanctified for hearers is to prepare the secret place of a pure mind for hearing, 389. The friend of God is one who hears His voice, 461.

The ears of the body ring when they are struck by an intolerable sound, 105. For the ears of minds an intolerable shout is the condemnation of some great sinner, ibid. The greatness of a poured-out voice is changed into ringing in the ears, ibid. What it means for both ears to ring, ibid., 106. The right ear signifies eternal life; the left, the present life, ibid. Why the ears of hearers alone are said to ring, 106.

The ear is revealed by the Lord when the preacher’s humble understanding is instructed by the Holy Spirit, 214. God inclines His ear to those who do not lift their necks, 513.

Aurora. Who are those rising like the dawn, 447.

Why the finest gold is called Christ’s head, 440. In gold the splendor of heavenly conduct is shown, 147. Every kind of metal is inferior to gold, 346, 440. Wisdom is expressed through gold, 414.

The south wind designates the Holy Spirit, 434.

We need God’s help in order to overcome the schemes of the wicked, 492. What must be obtained by persistent prayers, 493.

How many crimes avarice is the root of, 191. To decline after avarice is to pour oneself wholly downward through ambition for earthly things, ibid. Avarice is conquered by voluntary poverty, 303. Those who pursue avarice are reproved, 191.

To be turned away is from an equal…
not to be able to oppose by force, 129. The origins of the Ashdodites signify the beginnings of paganism, 138. What it means that the hand of the Lord was made heavy upon the Ashdodites, ibid. This heaviness of the hand is understood in the multiplication of converts, 139. When the hand of the Lord upon the Ashdodites was light, ibid. The hand of the Lord being made heavy upon the Ashdodites means the same as being killed by the bites of mice, ibid. Why the Ashdodites were struck in the innermost part of their nostrils, ibid. Ashdod had one day in hearing the preaching and another in attaining knowledge of the faith, 137. What it means for the ark of God to be brought into Ashdod, ibid.

## B

Babylon is weak in childbirth because, through disordered love of transitory things, she is unable to bear children, 60. What it means for Babylon to be constricted in childbirth, ibid. One becomes a citizen of Babylon through love of the world, 507. Who build Babylon, ibid. What it means to build Babylon out of bricks, ibid. What Babylon signifies, ibid.

Baptism prefigured by the Red Sea, 413. Whoever is reborn through baptism is redeemed from every sin by the grace of the Holy Spirit, 386. The Holy Spirit was directed from the circumcised to those baptized, ibid. Why each soul receives the Holy Spirit in baptism, 414, 430, 434, 502. The spring of the kid signifies baptism, 415. While the body is immersed, the soul is washed from all sins, ibid., 430, 434, 440. The newly baptized are signified by the flowers of the vineyards, 420, 421. Those washed in baptism ascend from the bath like a flock of shorn sheep, 428. Baptism is signified by Lebanon, 430, 434. Through Christ we believers are made white and exalted, 442. Our mother is regenerating grace, 446. The Church is nourished by grace as by a mother who gives birth, ibid. The Lord revealed to Nicodemus that no one would enter the kingdom without regeneration, [Col. 1431] 527. Through baptism we received light, 542.

The blessedness of the elect is signified when peace is shown as being made between them and the reprobate, 173. This is represented by the Psalter, 240. This is what must first be preached to the faithful, ibid. Holy souls, released from the body, enjoy heaven, 419. Blessedness is bestowed on holy souls before the resurrection, 499, 534; and on their bodies after the resurrection, ibid. Description of eternal blessedness, 558, 559. See *Happiness; Eternal life*.

For the blessed citizens, God is all in all, 88. Who are to be called blessed, 474. The blessed undergo a twofold transformation, 534. See *The saints in heaven*.

Those are called sons of Belial who, in their pride, do not obey their spiritual fathers, 82; and those who despise their superiors, 257. A powerful war is said to occur when harsh sons rule over elect peoples, 339. Who are weak for war, 338. Who are most highly trained for battles, 425. See *Combat*.

Saint Benedict, the excellent teacher of the strictest way of life and an instructed disciple of supreme truth, 199.

With what fruit the divine benefits bestowed on us should be remembered, 272. Whoever receives a benefit from God should hold one thing in his hands and see another with his eyes, 307.

Benjamin is interpreted as “son of the right hand,” 214, 222, 231. The land of Benjamin is the holy Church, 214. The clans of the tribe of Benjamin are the different ways of life of the elect, ibid. What the boundaries of Benjamin signify, 231.

Beersheba signifies the wise and the righteous, 110. Beersheba is interpreted as “seventh well,” ibid.

What is signified by the command that the beast, if it touches the mountain, must be stoned, 90, 399.

Beth-aven is interpreted as “house of vanity” or “useless house,” 285, 313. What it means to have a useless house in the eastern region of Michmash, ibid. What is signified by the battle carried as far as Beth-aven, 313.

Beth-car is interpreted as “house of the Lamb,” 170. Why no one can reach Beth-car, ibid. The place beneath Beth-car expresses the common fullness of holiness, ibid.

Bethel is interpreted as “House of God,” 174, 234, 279, 422. Bethel signifies men appointed to the office of the sacred altar, ibid. Bethel can also designate the universal Church of the elect, ibid. Who the three men ascending into Bethel are, 234. Those who defend the Church with the authority of the word guard Bethel, 280.

Bethlehem is interpreted as “house of bread,” 375. Bethlehem designates every house of religion, ibid. Why Samuel is sent to Bethlehem to anoint the king, 388.

Beth-horon is interpreted as “house of wrath,” 293. The house of wrath is a mind serving a contentious tongue, ibid.

Beth-shemesh is interpreted as “house of the sun,” 152. The house of the sun is the heavenly city, 156. The Ark ascends toward Beth-shemesh when, by walking, it does not leave the boundary road, ibid. The road of Beth-shemesh is narrow, ibid. Through the vice of open laxity we turn aside from the road of Beth-shemesh, 153. The boundaries of Beth-shemesh are knowledge of sacred discourse and good works, 154. These are boundaries because they both admit those worthy of contemplation and drive out those unworthy of it, ibid. How the Ark of God is brought to Beth-shemesh, 155. The Beth-shemites are understood as those who are already perfected men in the loftiness of contemplation, 154. Who are of the house of the sun, ibid. What is signified by the Beth-shemites reaping wheat in the valley, 155. [Col. 1432] What is signified by the Beth-shemites cutting the timbers of the cart, 157. On what day the Beth-shemites offer burnt offerings to the Lord and sacrifice victims, 158. The Beth-shemites who were struck signify heretics deceived by false contemplation, 160. The fear of the faithful, though simple-minded, at the striking of the erring Beth-shemites, ibid. The Beth-shemites who were struck also signify priests and sacred ministers handling the holy mysteries of the altar unworthily, ibid. The fear of the Beth-shemites can refer to the burden of ecclesiastical leadership, 162. The Beth-shemite men die when they look outwardly upon the Ark of God, ibid.

By despising vain goods one is rescued from true evils, 276. The vain and deceptive goods of the world, passing quickly away, deceive their lovers, 276. To turn aside after these goods is to prefer love of them to divine love, ibid. Good works are not all to be done by everyone, nor in every manner or at every time, 322. Goods mingled with evils are not pleasing to God, 474, 483. We are unable to appear good without elation, 299. Whoever imitates Christ pursues goodness, 492.

Bores is interpreted as “in primacy,” 303.

A cluster of bitterness is the fruit of the vineyard of Sodom, 196. The cluster brought from the land of promise prefigures Christ, 459.

What it means to take oxen as booty, 319. In the ox, the labor and strength of preaching are expressed, 320. To lead an ox by the hand is to wipe away the sin of pride through repentance, ibid. What is signified by an ox made from a calf, 26. Oxen signify preachers who plow the field of the Church, 308.

What is signified by the arm cut off from the Jews, 78. The arm of one who despises God is temporal strength, 88. The arm of the despiser and his father’s house are to be cut off, ibid. Operations are signified by the word “arm,” 456.

What the morsel of bread signifies, 81. The morsel of bread is the unfailing delight of eternal life, 94. What it means to sound the trumpet, 281.

## C
### C

The blindness of those who refuse to do the good they know, 96, 487. Not seeing is the punishment of the sinner who is still living in this world, 98, 114. Being unable to see is the eternal punishment of the impious who has been condemned, ibid. What slaughter is called “very great,” 312. The celibacy of the priests of the new law, not of the old, 69. By what error those who profess celibacy are deceived, 344. The chastity that clerics have cultivated is lost by many after they become priests, 358. Cain sinned against the Holy Spirit by despairing of forgiveness, 502. Shoes made from dead animals signify the examples of the Fathers who came before, 449. We spiritually put on shoes when we take examples from the deceased Fathers, ibid. Who is said to shoe the Church, ibid. What the Church’s shoes are, ibid. What Caleb and Joshua, the only Israelites who came out of Egypt to enter the promised land, signify, 535. The camel signifies the shepherd’s stooping as he crawls toward sinners, 307. What the camel chewing the cud and not dividing the hoof signifies, 344. What the bridle and bit signify, 480. Who are the mute dogs unable to bark, 97. Why they cannot bark even when they wish to, ibid.

Where the *Song of Songs* gets its name, [Col. 1433] 393, 400. Why it is third in the order of Solomon’s books, 401. The *Song* expounded by Jewish, Greek, and Latin teachers, 393. Why the *Song of Songs* was written allegorically, 397. How the words of carnal love used in it are to be understood, 398. The various kinds of songs in Holy Scripture, 400. The *Song of Songs* superior to the others, 393, 400. The union of Christ with the Church is celebrated in this Song, 401. The contemplative life is signified by the *Song of Songs*, ibid. In this Song the soul sees God’s entrance into its own heart, ibid. Four persons are introduced as speaking in the *Song of Songs*, ibid.

Hair signifies an abundance of earthly substance, 17. By the bride’s hair peoples are signified, 427. The valley of the does is the precious death of the saints, 294. The does signify the dignity of holy souls, ibid. What the valley of the does, situated opposite the desert, signifies, ibid. The doe is a clean animal according to the Law, 418. The doe figures the Church, 422. What the two fawns, twin offspring of a doe, signify, 450. Who has his head sprinkled with dust, 131. Heads signify the minds of the subject people, 202. To incline the head is for spiritual men to lower their mind from the highest contemplation, 236. Who the foundations of the earth are, 51, 63.

Cariathiarim means “their city,” 161. Carmel means “soft” or “tender,” 354. By “tender” the inexperienced person in holy conduct is signified, ibid. “Soft” signifies those who, through the practice of virtue, have not been made firm in the goodness they have begun, ibid. Carmel also means “knowledge of circumcision,” 451. What it means to raise the sign of victory on Carmel, 354. Why Christ is compared with Carmel, 451. What it means to pray on Carmel, ibid.

The carnal mind is not taken up to contemplation, 34. The carnal mind is affected by love of bodily things, ibid. The serpent opens the eyes of the carnal, 177. For the carnal, every submission is most burdensome, since they are slaves of their own will, 180. Often the carnal appear to accomplish great things in the Church, 188. The carnal do not possess the grace of the Holy Spirit by which their hard heart may be softened, ibid. An invading spirit changes a carnal man into another man, 243. People marvel at this change, whose cause they do not understand, 248. The carnal are pricked by fear, 273. It belongs to the carnal and the simple to wonder at new things that occur beyond ordinary usage, 308. In the Church the carnal inopportunely rouse those resting in contemplation of the mind of the Bridegroom, 418. The carnal are called “daughters,” ibid. The carnal are prefigured by the pelican and the night-raven, 516. When the carnal speak of heavenly things, they use them like sick people using things they are forbidden to taste, 206. The exaltation of the carnal is the cause of many evils, 184. In a virginal body carnal impulses have no repose of pleasure, but remain in a state of combat, 281. Those who advance the carnal to the summit of the Church sin most gravely, 279.

What raw flesh signifies, 68. To sow in the flesh is to bury the mind’s purpose in bodily pleasures, 195. In the affliction of the flesh discretion must be maintained, 153. Flesh is said to be “unfolded” when it is not burdened by the moisture of fatness through abstinence, 259. How to mock the flesh by promising it certain future advantages, 261, 265. The illicit impulses of the flesh cannot be extinguished, but must be mitigated by fasts, 267. They must be overcome so that two things do not remain together: an impure thought and the natural impulse of the flesh, ibid. If the shameful impulse is not removed from the flesh, at least the strength of the shamefulness must be weakened, 342. Those who declare war on the vices of the flesh must excel in strength and teaching, 346. The flesh’s warfare is severe, 349. The king of his own flesh is adorned with hope of immortality, 441, 444. Flesh consists of four elements, 467. Flesh watered by tears brings forth the seedling of good works, 471. Soft things nourish the flesh, and hard things strengthen the soul, 490. Flesh signifies the weak in the Church, 514.

Perfect chastity is the proof of true abstinence, 266. Illicit impulses cannot be removed from the flesh, 267. They can be diminished, and their pleasure taken away, ibid. They must be resisted, and we must grieve over them, ibid. An impure thought and the natural impulse of the flesh must not remain together, ibid. The retinue of chaste thoughts, 331. The examples of chastity are the footprints of the heavenly soldiers impressed upon the earth, 345. Lofty chastity and unclean humility are both displeasing to God, 483. Conjugal chastity, 344, 347.

By chance is meant what happens suddenly and without deliberation or foresight, 153. The cleft in the wall signifies the wound in Christ’s side, 420. It also signifies the protection of angelic guardianship, ibid. Cedar means “darkness,” 409. Cedar was the second-born of the race of Ishmael, ibid. Kedar was the tents of Esau, ibid. Cedar signifies the tents of the Gentiles and of darkness, 410. The cedar is a very lofty tree, fragrant and incorruptible, 442.

The discretion of ecclesiastical discipline in the faults of subjects, whether they are to be corrected or disregarded, 258. In ecclesiastical discipline, although there is no respect of persons, there is nevertheless discrimination according to merits, 328. The number one hundred signifies perfection, 183. It contains the total sum of numbers, 292. In the number one hundred the whole sum of the Decalogue is included, 345. A centurion is named from the number one hundred, 183. Centurions are more perfect men who, well instructed by preachers, become their co-workers, 193. They are eminent in action and instructed in knowledge of the word of God, ibid. Centurions are appointed so that they may live sublimely, and the higher they live, the more usefully may they teach, ibid.

The spiritual battles of Christians, 125, 268. The Jews falsely thought that they had a battle with the devil, ibid. The fields of battle are the verdant meanings of sacred eloquence, 127. The teachers of the Church, fighting against the Jews, easily dissolve and ridicule their devices, 129. How great battles those recently converted endure against demons, 167. When devoted to inward meditation, we fight against the enemy more successfully, 170. How far we must pursue him, ibid. By unceasing effort in battle we must strive toward the citadel of perfection, ibid. The ancients used to fight from chariots, 192. Thus raised aloft, we should exercise our strength for battle, ibid. Who fight from the chariot in spiritual combat, ibid. Who are the horsemen in this battle, ibid. Who are the tribunes and centurions, 193. Who are said to be the pursuers of royal chariots, ibid. The foot soldiers are on level ground, slow to run and weak in combat, 193. The elect, placed in those chariots and arms, are swift and powerful, 194. Those who are to be led into spiritual battle must first be tested by their commander, 263. The spiritual battles of the elect, 268. God wishes the elect always to remain in battle, 281. How many battles must be undertaken by those inflamed with desire for the better life, 298. The place of battle is the heart of one listening to the word of God, 311. What it means to fight every day, 339. See *War*.

The stag is a clean animal according to the law, 418. By stags and does faith, hope, and charity are understood, ibid. By stags the ancient Fathers are meant, from whom Christ is designated as a fawn, 422. The Canaanite woman deserved to be heard because she did not cease crying out, 538.

The gift of charity is rightly figured under the name of wine, 26. A wine-jar signifies the beginning of charity, 27. Who are to be admitted to the banquet of charity, 223. The beauty of the face is itself the beauty of charity, 383. Other virtues are the body of justice; charity is the face of this body, ibid. Charity is signified by the broad commandment, 407. The beginnings and progress of charity, 451. The charity of martyrs must be overwhelmed neither by many waters nor by rivers, 457. Charity is overwhelmed when it is turned into hatred against persecutors, ibid. The rivers are consumed by charity itself, ibid. Everything must be despised for the sake of charity, 457. Charity is the mother of the virtues, 479.

Who truly possesses charity, 472. The perfection of charity is attained through worthy struggles, 53. From the beginning of fear we are led to the bond of great charity, 263. Through long practice charity teaches us to reject all created things from our intention and to rejoice in the vision of eternal majesty, 53. His charity is true who loves his friend in God and his enemy for God’s sake, 472. When charity burns in the heart, it emits a cry, 486. Charity is kind, 540. Charity is ordered by Holy Scripture, 417. See *Love*, *Affection*.

### Cherubim

What it means to ascend to the Lord by means of the Cherubim, 25.

The spiritual battles of Christians, 125. Christians are taught to trample the head and arms of Dagon, 138. Christians are especially bound to fear God by avoiding evil and to serve him in truth by doing good, 278. The three kinds of Christians who follow God, 406. Christians feed the young goats beside the shepherds’ tents by faith, not by works, 413. Christians serving desires are the priests of Dagon, 138. A Christian prefers to be killed rather than conquered, 491.

Christ as a man surrounded by a woman, 7. Why he is called “man,” ibid., 65. Why he is called “one man,” ibid. This unity of Christ belongs not only to his person but also to his excellence, 8. Christ is the tree whose fruits are the elect, 10. Christ is our peace, 64, 173, 389. Christ is called the cornerstone, 65, 171, 524. Christ is called bread, 81. The door, 134, 459. The great stone, 157. Christ is the stone of help for the elect; he shatters and crushes the reprobate, 171. Christ is the suckling lamb, 168. Why he is called one and whole as a lamb, ibid. Christ is called the Son of the right hand, 214.

The figure of Christ is Elkanah, 5. Why Christ, under the name Elkanah, is said to have been from Ramathaim-zophim of Mount Ephraim, 8. What it means for Christ to ascend from his own city, 10. And on appointed days, 11. Joshua the Bethshemite figures Christ in name and dignity, 156. Kish figures Christ, 203. Benjamin also figures Christ, 214, 231. Christ is designated by the name “hill,” 239. The hill of the son of the right hand is the eternal exaltation of the Redeemer, 291. Christ is understood under the name “pomegranate,” 300. Christ is signified by the name Ahitub, 301. What Ahitub, the brother of Ichabod, figures, ibid. Christ is called the great stone, 320. Also the rolled stone, one part of which displays humility and the other exaltation, ibid. What it means for the ox and the ram to be killed on this stone, ibid. Christ is signified by the name Ahimaaz, 337. Christ is our beauty, ibid. Christ is figured in David, 386. Christ is the beginning and the end, [Col. 1435] ibid., 531. Christ is called “strong of hand,” ibid., 429. Christ is as though anointed when the fragrance of his reputation is disclosed to those who do not know him, ibid. Christ is anointed with a full horn, 387. Christ is designated by the name of a calf, 388. Christ is called little, 390. And Shepherd, ibid. Christ is food for blessed souls and angels, ibid. How Christ is red and beautiful in appearance, ibid., 391. Christ is called the bridegroom, 402. The sun, 409. Why he is called a flower, 416. In Christ alone we find the food of salvation, ibid. Christ is called the apple among the woodland trees, ibid. The shadow of Christ is the protection of the Holy Spirit, ibid. Christ is the fruitful tree to be cultivated in our hearts, 417. Christ is like a doe, 418.

Why Christ is proclaimed to be like a fawn among stags, 419, 422, 462. Solomon is a figure of Christ, 425. David, strong of hand, figures Christ, 429. Why Christ is the beloved from the beloved, 439. Christ is white through innocence and ruddy through suffering, 140, 498. Why he is chosen out of thousands, ibid. Why he is chosen like a cedar, 442. Christ is wholly desirable, ibid. He is called Aminadab, 449. He is called peaceful, 459. He is called a cluster of grapes, ibid. The beloved is compared with a doe, 462. He is called the omnipotent physician, for whom no wound is incurable, 494. Christ is the high priest of future good things, 498. Christ is called “Salvific,” 502. “Rising,” 507. “Rock,” 509. What it means that Christ was the pelican of the wilderness, 517. Christ was the night-raven when he evangelized the kingdom of God to those who were in darkness, ibid. Christ is called the lion’s cub, 517. Christ is stronger than the strong armed man, ibid. Christ is the solitary sparrow on the roof, ibid. Christ is the man who sows, 519. Savior and defender, 525. Christ is called “Most High,” 527. “Holy,” ibid. “Heaven,” ibid. Christ is the seat of God, the heaven of God, 528. The first and the last, 531. Christ is the propitiation for our sins, 540. How Christ is the firstborn from the dead, 511. The open fountain of the house of David is Christ, 544. Christ is the wisdom of God, 557. Christ is the tree of salvation in the sea of a stormy tempest, ibid.

Christ assumed our nature in order to strengthen these weak things in himself, 6. In Christ there is not one person of the Word who assumed and another of the man who was assumed, 7. Christ’s pre-eminence, ibid. Manhood is the time of the Lord’s Incarnation, 79. The age preceding the Incarnation of the Word was the infancy of the world, ibid. If Adam had not sinned, Christ would not have been incarnate, 179. The Lord was anointed with the oil of gladness when he became incarnate, 403. The Lord was incarnate through the agency of the Holy Spirit, ibid. In the Incarnation the breasts of God were brought near to us, ibid. The preaching of the Incarnation is far superior to the counterfeit wisdom of the world, ibid. The poured-out ointment is the incarnate divinity, 405. In rushing into the embraces of the bride, Christ, through the Incarnation, crossed what mountains and hills, 418. God hidden in the flesh lay concealed as though behind a wall, 419. Through windows and lattices he sometimes looked forth, performing wonders and enduring hardships, 419. The mysteries of the Incarnation are signified by the openings in the rock, 420. Through the Incarnation Christ was crowned with a diadem, 427. The day of betrothal is the day of the Incarnation, ibid. The Incarnation of the Word was foreknown by David, 496, 498. It is praiseworthy that God formed man from the clay of the earth; more praiseworthy that he redeemed what was lost by the death of the Son, 505. The Incarnation of the Word of God was truly our glory, 427.

Christ was to be born from the Jewish people according to the flesh, 388. Christ’s birth from the Virgin was given as a sign of the spiritual birth of human beings from God that was to come, 527. He became our warrior and our Creator, 6. Christ speaks and acts in his ministers, spreading the good fragrance of life, 123. Why Christ says that the day of judgment is known by no one, not even by the Son, 118. Christ did not wish to be born from unbelievers, 9.

Christ’s miracles are marked by appointed days, 11. The excellence of the four cardinal virtues in Christ, 9. Those whom he taught by living, Christ redeemed by dying, 11. The difference between Christ’s miracles and those of the patriarchs and prophets of the ancient Law, 45. The prophets were taught by Christ, 46. Christ fasted for forty days and forty nights, 266. What someone preaching Christ must learn, 388. Why the promises concerning Christ placed in Holy Scripture are called appointed days, 11. As many promises of Christ as there are in the Law and the Prophets, so many appointed days are there for his ascent, ibid. Christ alone is without sin, 459, 477, 497, 502. Christ’s exceptional holiness, 44. All the saints are made holy through his gift, ibid. The angels themselves are believed to have been sanctified in the Son, ibid. The beauty of holiness is called the beauty of his face, 391.

Christ fulfilled the will of his Father both by living and by dying, 12. No one was harsher toward himself than Christ, 203. Let us learn patience from Christ, 489. When accused, Christ remained silent, ibid. Christ provided incentives to patience, 490. Christ’s patience toward the Jews is figured by David’s patience toward his son Absalom, 545. Christ is humble and obedient as an example for the elect, 11. How great Christ is, and how humble, 320. His example of humility is to be set before preachers desirous of empty glory, ibid. Christ became poor and humble for us, 462. Christ, our head, deigned to assume the weaknesses and sufferings of his members, 488. The mediator of God and human beings came for this purpose: to offer us an example of humility and patience, 489. By imitating Christ’s humility and suffering we obtain forgiveness, 498. Christ assumed the necessities of our poverty so that he might make us participants in his riches, 510.

Christ, through his mercy toward sinners, seemed to crawl on his hands, 307. In Christ it was not the harshness of the law but singular mercy that shone forth, 387. May the multitude of mercies aid one afflicted by many illnesses, 494. The difference and definition of mercy and compassion, ibid. Christ displayed innumerable acts of mercy to the world, rescuing people from the slavery of the devil, 495. Christ’s mercy toward tax collectors and sinners, 519, 543. The immeasurable mercy of the Son of God dying for sinners, 544.

Christ is fed by good works, 435. What his banquets and delights are, ibid. At Christ’s banquet some merely eat, while others are also intoxicated, ibid. When Christ visits the saints, he makes them more ardent in his love, 443. Christ’s food and drink are the progress of the elect, 519, and the conversion of sinners, 520. Christ prays for us by presenting himself to the Father in human flesh, 26. God became man as intercessor for those for whom no human being was sufficient, 73. God was reconciled, not by another’s prayer but by his own, to those who had sinned against him, ibid. He was reconciled not to everyone but to certain people, ibid. Christ prays for the Church, 511. He intercedes for us, 540. The head prays for the members: Christ for the Church, 545.

Christ’s members, afflicted through penitence, are Solomon’s skins, 410. Who is said to have a vigilant heart while Christ sleeps, 436. God is Christ’s head, ibid., 440. Why his head is called the finest gold, ibid. A description of Christ’s hands, 441. Why his hands are full of hyacinths, ibid. Why Christ’s belly is called ivory, 441. “Distinguished by sapphires” signifies Christ’s mortality adorned with miracles, 442. Why Christ’s appearance is said to be like Lebanon, ibid. Christ’s members speak the words of their head as though they were their own, 487. Great consolation for the members: that Christ our head becomes a participant in our suffering, 488. Christ’s feet, that is, the Apostles, were moved in his passion, 490. Who are signified by Christ’s bones, and who by his flesh, 514. How the bones of Christ’s body may dry up like a potsherd, ibid. So that we may avoid dryness, let us cling to Christ the head, 522. Christ is still afflicted in his body, 512.

Christ is true God, 42. Christ proved himself God by incomparable miracles, 44, 45, 73. In the Redeemer there is the incomparability of the divine essence, ibid. The one to whom the Redeemer’s divinity is revealed is set upon high places, 52. The Lord’s humanity was assumed by his divinity, 67. The Jews suggested to the faithful that they deny the Redeemer’s divinity, 68. But the Church refused, promising the food of divinity, ibid. Christ, God and man, is signified by the rolled stone, 320. The splendor of eternal divinity is called the beauty of the face, 390.

Christ is far greater than Moses and Abraham, 43. They were taken up for ministry; the only-begotten one was taken up for kingship, 44. In the assertion that he is Lord, the excellence of his holiness is commended, ibid. How much Christ surpasses the other saints, 389. Christ’s beauty and loveliness, 390. Now we see Christ’s back parts, so that we may follow him; afterward we shall see his front, ibid. In order to reach Christ, all human beings must be passed beyond, 423, 467.

Christ is the Father’s Word and Lord of all knowledge, 46. The prophets were taught by Christ, ibid. Christ is judge not only of the tongue but also of the heart, 47. The Father gave his judgment to the Son as king, 525. Christ alone is free from the hand of the Philistines, separated from sinners, 165, 440, 497, 502.

Christ’s horn will be exalted when the elect have been gathered into heavenly glory, 53. The Lord’s kingdom is always equal when it is exalted, 54. Peter saw Christ’s glory imperfectly on the mountain, 391. No one should dare to preach that glory unless he is raised toward heavenly things, 392. Why we are commanded to turn our eyes away from Christ’s blessedness, 444. What the eyes of the mind are that cause Christ to fly away from us, ibid.

Christ’s priesthood excluded the old priesthood, 78. After rejecting the priests of the synagogue, Christ appointed the faithful as priests for himself, 79. They obeyed his will, 80. Through Christ we believers are made white and exalted, 442. Christ is set before us as the model of justice, for us to imitate, 490, 498. He walks before Christ who proposes his example to himself for imitation in everything he does, 80. How Christ conquers when he is judged, 497. Christ is the end and consummation of the Law and the Prophets, 466. Christ is the perfection of all good things, 467.

Christ was abandoned by his own while enemies inflicted violence, 488. With what glory those are crowned who glorified Christ, 77. To know Christ without loving him is useless, 389. The nearer Christ approaches us, the more he shows us our foulness, 409. Who are Christ’s friends and who are especially dear to him, 435. These may be called Christ’s heart, 436. No one is dear to Christ unless he delights in the Holy Scriptures, 451.

How great Christ’s kindness toward his bride, the Church, is, 507. This kindness is entirely gratuitous, ibid. Christ’s kindness toward sinners and unbelievers gives us hope of obtaining forgiveness, [Col. 1437] 519. Let us remain in him who remains forever, 540. We cannot bear fruit unless we remain in him, ibid.

Christ’s works, which he set before us for imitation, are designated by his hands, 441. They are “turned” because of their perfect justice, ibid. They are golden because of the divinity from which they proceeded, ibid. Whoever returns insults for insults becomes an exile from Christ’s teaching, 489. How Christ is justified in his sayings, 497. What Christ cries out in the wilderness, in the dwelling, and on the roof, 517.

Christ regarded his persecutors as assistants in the paternal command imposed upon him, 13. The Jews killed Christ so that the whole world would not go after him, 48. The whole world went after him because, once killed, he came to life again, ibid. The bow of the mighty was overcome through the Resurrection, Ascension, and sending of the Holy Spirit, ibid. Christ’s victory over the Jews, 490.

What Christ fulfilled is of no avail unless it is fulfilled by the one who completes what remained, 224. The imitators of Christ must be not human beings but beings above human beings, 399. How Christ is a bundle of myrrh for his imitators, 415. Eternal happiness remains for the imitators of Christ, 441. Let the sign of Christ be placed upon the heart and upon the arm, 456. Whoever follows the ways of Christ’s passion is whitened above the snow, 499. The way of Christ’s virtue is imitation of his steadfastness, 531.

Dying, Christ weakened the powers of hell, 7. Christ wished to be known for this purpose: that by dying he might redeem those whom he had taught by living, II. The Father’s command that Christ should die was imposed upon him, 12. Christ’s passion was figured by Elkanah’s sacrifice, 13. The bread cooked on a griddle is the Redeemer’s flesh afflicted by punishments, 81. One suckling lamb is offered because apart from Christ, who takes away sins, no one is found, 168. Christ graciously assumed for us what was harsh toward himself and what he could suffer, 203. As Christ went toward his passion, why did he sit upon the released she-ass and its colt, ibid. By whom Christ was anointed in the tomb, 336. For Christ, to die is to rest, and to sleep is to sleep, 436. Christ, dying on the cross, raised up the Church, 456. Christ suffered in the strength of his love toward us, 457. Christ’s passion is to be imitated by us, 498. That God formed man from the clay of the earth belongs to power; that he redeemed what was lost by the death of the Son belongs to grace, 505. Christ was anxious for us, handed over to death, and hung upon the wood, 510. How the skin, once the flesh had been consumed, clung to Christ’s bone, 514. The dead killed life, 517. Christ the Lion reclined in rest, ibid. To Christ suffering for us we must respond by suffering with him, 530.

Rising again, Christ opened the way to eternity for us, 7, 541. Those whom Christ found among the dead he brought back to the joys of Paradise, 13. Elkanah and his whole household ascending to sacrifice the solemn offering signify the triumph of Christ’s Ascension, 23. When human nature was raised above the angels, the horn of the Church was exalted, 41. Through the resurrection Christ triumphed over the savagery of the Jews, 47. The Jews should not despise Christ because he was able to die; rather, they should marvel that he rose again, 48. The risen Christ appears to the disciples living in seclusion, 234. How much the Church benefited from Christ’s Ascension, 414. When and what kind of Christ, who is absent through the Ascension, returned to us, 422. Christ’s mortality passed into immortality by rising again, 441. By rising again Christ carried away victory over the Jews, 490, 497. Christ slept in death and kept watch in the resurrection, 517. [Col. 1437] 541. Christ’s glory is the resurrection, 524. The power of Christ is the glory of his resurrection, 529. Christ died and rose again so that, dead to sins, we might live to righteousness, 556. Before his death Christ fled glory; after his death he wished to be known, 320. Christ draws us to himself both by his commandments and by the examples of the saints, 420.

What taking food, and taking food afterward, signify, 15. Often we use food not for nourishment but for pleasure, 33. What the food of the elect soul is, 38, 67. This food is cooked in sacred vessels, ibid. The food of the soul is the word of God, 206. The feeling of devotion is food for the mind, 211. How food should be given to the body, 260. Let us work for food that endures unto eternal life, 535. What decayed scars signify, 484.

What the locks of the Bridegroom’s head, full of drops of night, signify, 437. By the Bridegroom’s locks peoples are to be understood, ibid. The sinner is like ashes, 519. How Christ eats these ashes, ibid.

### Circuit

We have enemies all around us who lie in wait for us from every side, 329. How we may conquer these same enemies all around us, ibid. What the cycle of days signifies, 23, 39.

The generation of Kish is mentioned so that the royal dignity founded in his son may be shown not to endure, 188. Kish means “hard,” ibid. Why he is called hard through strength of power, ibid., 201, 202. Kish signifies the elect and the Redeemer himself, 203, 231. He also signifies good shepherds, 231. What Kish and Ner, sons of one father, signify, 338.

The harp signifies the word of consolation for the elect, 240. The harp follows the flute so that we may mourn the hardships of exile in such a way that we rejoice in the promise of the eternal inheritance, ibid.

By what way the heavenly citizens came to the vision of God, 221. Citizens benefit their fellow citizens by doing good, 327. Everyone is either a citizen of Jerusalem or of Babylon, 507.

What the Redeemer’s city is, 10. A city is called a fortified place of those dwelling together, 33. What this city signifies, ibid. What it means to sit in the city, ibid. What it means to return to one’s own city, 38. What each city crying out to heaven signifies, 143. The house of the sun is the heavenly city, 156. Walled cities are minds surrounded by instruction in the Scriptures, 159. The city of the saints is Jerusalem above, 161. The man of God is to be sought in the city, 208. The teacher is in the city when he remains, through the ministry of preaching, in the instruction of the people subject to him, 209. When the preacher is in the city, and when he is on high, 210. Humility is the gate of this city, 216. The four parts of the city, that is, the Church, 227. The outermost part of the city is the last part of the people subject to it, ibid. Penitents are in the outermost part of the city, that is, of the Church, ibid. By the city the Church is understood; by the city’s lanes, spiritual men, 423. By its streets, secular men, ibid.

Jerusalem above is called the city of peace, 508, 558. A description of this city, ibid., 558. The walls of this city are built from chosen living stones, 508. Solomon’s temple bore the figure of this city, ibid.

Whose cry is said to have ascended to heaven, 143. The cry of the heart is fervent devotion, 168, 486. The shepherd’s cry is the devout request for the salvation of his subjects, 274. What the people’s cry after Saul, at the sound of the trumpet, signifies, 281. What it means for the shepherd to cry all night, [Col. 1438] 353. How someone cries wrongly in two ways all day long, 475. Crying signifies sin, ibid. Crying is sometimes taken in a good sense and sometimes in a bad sense, 511. The cry of the righteous and the cry of the impious, ibid. What Christ cries out in the wilderness, in the dwelling, and on the roof, 517.

Let him ascend the slope of the city who is about to approach the Seer, 209. We ascend the slope when we do not set before ourselves the level ground of weak hearers as an example, ibid.

Scarlet twice dyed in the high priest’s garment signifies double charity, 382. By scarlet the flame of charity is understood, 428. The cooks are priests, 223. See *Cook*.

The Apostles are designated by the name of the heavens, 53, 532, 549. We are heavens when we are lifted into the height of the divine grace presiding over us, 64. The thunderings of the heavens are the perfect desires of the elect, ibid. How the works of God’s hands are heavens, 532, 549. How the heavens will perish, 533. Heaven would be open to no one unless the Son of God had taken flesh for our salvation, 509. By what steps one ascends into heaven, 536.

The coenobites are instructed by the example of the boy Samuel, 85. The merit of the coenobites is to be measured by obedience, 101.

The subtle deliberation of an illicit thought is compared with dust, 62. Not only words but also thoughts are judged by God, 58. What it means to think for the sake of sin, 94. The very crowds of our thoughts are our flocks, 198. The thoughts of the mind must be subjected to Christ, ibid. How spiritual thought is fruitful, 208. The way of Ephraim, that is, of the fruitful heart, is good thought, 293. Our enemies lie in wait for our good thoughts, ibid. The mind’s guard against lustful thoughts, 331. Why these thoughts are compared with straw, 343. If we meet wicked thoughts head-on, lust is easily overcome, 351. Thoughts are signified by the name “heart,” 456. We are not sufficient to think anything good by ourselves, 551. Through evil thoughts the demon rests in the heart, 164. We cannot think two things at once, 351.

In what ways knowledge of heavenly things is acquired, 102. A person’s chief concern should be to know himself, 412. It is a clear sign of coming salvation if a person begins to know himself, 494, 549. It is not things but transgression of the prohibition concerning things that defiles a person, 566.

Sacred Scripture is like a neck, 237. Christ is designated by the name “hill,” 239. A hill is not a summit but the height of mountains near the summit, 293. The hill signifies the perfect life of faithful subjects, ibid. A hill is found in the law of the Lord, 239.

The neck signifies speech, 202. He has a neck above others who surpasses the rest in loftiness of speech, ibid. What the bride’s neck, like necklaces, signifies, 414, 528. The neck signifies the joining of the members of the Church to their head, 431, 528. This joining is faith, ibid. The bride’s neck signifies preachers, 450.

What the doves at their windows signify, 268, 299. Who the eyes of the doves are, 415. The dove groans in love instead of singing, ibid., 485. In the holes of the rock, the simple soul is strengthened in Christ’s wounds, 420. What the doves upon streams of water signify, 440. What doves washed in milk figure, ibid. One dove is called the Church of the elect, 446. Because of its simplicity the dove figures the soul that is Christ’s bride, 419. [Col. 1439]

The golden columns signify the Apostles, 442. The locks of the head are the thoughts of the mind, 451. By Christ’s locks we understand each of the faithful, 440. What it means for the locks to be bound among the carnal, 451.

For victors, to eat is to receive with pleasure the food of empty praise after a good work has been completed, 314. Let us abstain from such eating until evening, so that we may safely be refreshed at the end of the day, 315. What it means to eat with blood, 319.

### To lend

Whatever we lend, we expect to have returned to us in the faith of the recipient, 29.

The shaking of the earth signifies the grief of penitence, 143.

### Communion

Those who do not examine themselves before receiving the Eucharist are thereby deprived of the power of the sacrament, 59. They are not filled unless they are hungry, ibid. To examine oneself is, after the wickedness of sins has been emptied out, to present oneself pure at the Lord’s table, 60.

The fettered are understood in two ways, 528. The tears of compunction, 38. The benefit of compunction is understood when we rejoice unspeakably in confidence in divine forgiveness, 145. Those whom God wounds through compunction he heals through the security of forgiveness, 146. While the mind is pierced by weeping, the flesh too must be afflicted, 166. By the very tears of compunction let us seek not the favor of the world but only the fruit of divine reconciliation, ibid. The Holy Spirit, entering in, instills the devout tears of compunction, 242. The grace of compunction is not poured into the mind unless the greatness of sin has first been shown to it, 274. By the name “altar” the compunction of the heart is understood, 321. In us there are two altars,
- One must be built from a twofold compunction, ibid.
- Compunction is described as arising from love, 404.
- The soul kisses God as often as it is pierced by love of him, ibid.
- One who is pierced by the inward ardor of the mind is preferred to one who gives away his external possessions, ibid.
- Compunction ought to be frequent, ibid.
- The solemn day for the Lord is the compunction of our heart, ibid.
- The mind pierced by love is fed with the food of angels, 417.
- The fraternal concord of Jews and Gentiles in the faith of their fathers, 450.
- Why eighty concubines signify wicked preachers, 445.
- Secular desires are compared with prostitutes, 84.
- Secular desire is the grape of a reprobate mind, 173.

- The saints, raised to heavenly things through contemplation, discover and correct whatever vice lay hidden within them, 506.

- Those contend with God in judgment who either complain that they have been scourged by him or that they have not been heard, 546.

- Conversion begins with fear and disturbance, 309.
- In the conversion of sinners, God accomplishes some things directly and others through human beings, [Col. 1441] ibid.

- Converted sinners take care to call others to penance, 503.

- See the Conversion of Sinners, and also Saint Paul.

- Marital intercourse, by divine institution, is good, 497.
- Carnal pleasure is the punishment of sin, ibid.
- What it means to cook flesh, 67.
- To believe that the Lord’s humanity, assumed into divinity, is offered to God is to cook flesh, ibid.
- A priest is signified by the term “cook,” 223.
- See Cook.
- The heart should be fortified by the guardianship of perfect vigilance, 33.
- The mind has placed its heart in God through the joy of extraordinary devotion, 54.
- The reprobate does not possess his own heart, because the devil possesses it, ibid.
- The heart must be prepared for God, 164.
- Purity of heart should be joined to bodily continence, 169.

- The transformation of the heart is no less a miracle than the disturbance of the air, 274.
- The heart of one negligent in the spiritual life is compared with the shore of the sea, 283.
- Evil spirits encamp in hearts not kindled with love of heavenly things, 284.
- In sacred Scripture, “heart” is used for the will, 290.
- The saints can scarcely find their own heart, 325.
- How much less can the imperfect, ibid.
- The eyes of the heart are the sight of reason, 357.
- Those who grow proud lose the eyes of the heart, ibid.
- The hardness of a cast-off heart, 367.
- What it means to believe with the heart unto righteousness, ibid.
- The steadfast heart of one subjected to temptations is signified as unshaken, 376.
- How the heart becomes a censer before God, 425.
- How we ought to open our heart to Christ, 438.
- The hardness of the heart is wonderfully and sweetly dissolved by the Holy Spirit infused into the soul, ibid.

- The eye of the heart is soiled by earthly love, 457.
- One must cry out to God with the voice of the heart, 486.
- How our heart is to be cleansed, 501.
- The heart is crushed in vain unless it is humbled, 506.
- Our body is the temple of God; the heart is the altar, 509.
- Lust produces blindness of heart, 357.
- What it means to walk before Christ, 80.
- Peter is reproved by Jewish believers because he received Cornelius into the faith, 410.
- The horn of Hannah is the power of the holy Church, 41.
- That our horn has been exalted in our God, 42, 56.
- What it means for Christ’s horn to be raised up, 53.
- The horn signifies the intention of the elect mind, 55.
- It is raised when fixed in God and lowered in passing goods, ibid.
- He has an exalted horn in God who enjoys the lofty vision of inward light, ibid.
- To strike with the horn is to rebuke sinners sharply, 375.
- What it means for the horn to be filled with oil, ibid.
- The horn is the teacher’s spiritual way of life, ibid.
- What it means for the horn of oil to be taken away, 384.
- A horn full of oil signifies the sharpness of discipline and the anointing of grace, ibid.
- The sharpness of the horn signifies the austerity of the Law, [Col. 1442] 387.
- The horn of Christ’s kingdom signifies the sublimity of the Church, ibid.
- The horn of salvation is the sublimity of ecclesiastical power, ibid.
- He who has this horn erect and full of oil, ibid.
- The horn signifies the mind’s affection, 388.
- The horn is filled when the holiness of Christ is rightly recognized, ibid.
- Christ is anointed with a full horn when he is preached most perfectly, ibid.
- The horn of the altar is the exaltation of the inward sacrifice. Through the horns of the calves we note the precepts of both Testaments, 510.
- We produce horns if we strive to please God in the things belonging to the flesh, ibid.
- The horn is understood in many ways, 384, 388.
- Those who refresh the body without the mind are dead in mind but alive in flesh, 218.
- How many and how great are the troubles of the body arising from sin, 482.
- No part of our body remains untouched by vices, 485.
- Our body is the temple of God; the heart is the altar, 509.

- Sinners should be reproved in such a way that no avenue of escape is left to them, 357.
- Corrected sinners are like serpents, 358.
- Charity should lie hidden beneath the harshness of correction, 384.

- The day of tomorrow is the coming of the divine visitation, 264.

- Those appear to grow who are without the Lord, ibid.
- A crime is one thing, a sin another, 321, 566.
- We can avoid the former entirely; we cannot wholly erase the latter, ibid.
- What it signifies to eat a raw lamb, 67.
- What it means for the lamb to be cooked in water, ibid.
- Christ’s cross prepares heavenly food, 452.
- Christ’s cross is figured by the palm, ibid.
- Ascending the cross like a palm, Christ offered us its fruit, ibid.
- From this we are intoxicated with charity, ibid.
- The cross is signified by a tree, 456.
- How much is granted to those who suffer the cross, 14.
- A chamber is the more private part of a house, 424.
- After casting away the burdens of the world, spiritual men make a chamber for the Bridegroom, ibid.
- Those who seize the summit of the Church falsely judge that God has handed over to oblivion the plunder of the summit they invaded, on account of certain things they themselves have done bravely, 279.
- By what path access to the summit of the Church is open, 376.
- Let no one unworthy of any dispensation be permitted to come to the summit of the religious life, 381.
- A fault that cannot rightly be struck with severity is to be concealed, not exposed, 258.
- The fault must first be discovered, and punishment then imposed, 323.
- The matter must be examined at length so that the fault may be discovered, ibid.
- Not all faults are to be struck with the same severity, 324.
- Even when serious faults are to be punished, account must be taken of the offenders, ibid., 327.
- The weakness or strength of each individual must be investigated, 325.
- Faults should not be struck on the basis of conjectures, but carefully investigated, 326.
- A fault known through certain clear indications must not be judged before it has been demonstrated with complete clarity, ibid.
- Faults should be weighed not by respect for persons but in relation to the former life, 327.

- One oppressed by worldly cares can never order spiritual things, 225.
- One must withdraw from worldly cares in order to seek Christ, 422.
- The mind free from worldly cares is Christ’s little bed, 425.
- A cure acquired with difficulty is guarded more carefully, 470.

- What sort of chariot must be prepared for battle, 194.

- Those who neglect care of themselves devote themselves wholly to guarding what is near them, ibid.

- What the morning watch signifies, 541, 542.
- The guardianship of God’s judgments, 542.
- What riches must be guarded by one who has reached the light, ibid.

- Cyneus signifies married couples, ibid.
- What the cypress signifies, 416.
- Cyprus is an island on which more abundant vineyards grow, 415.

## D

Demons are called mighty, 58. Demons are represented by mice, 139. Foreign gods are so called, 164. The imperfect desires of Christians do not frighten demons, 169. They are frightened by the devotion of the elect and struck down by their works, 170. Demons serve holy men in many ways, 196. Their being conquered by the elect increases their condemnation, ibid. See *Devil*, *Evil angels*.

Dagon lying face down on the ground before the ark: what it signifies, 137. The ark set up beside Dagon: what it signifies, ibid. One who lies face down on the ground presses his face into the earth, ibid. The face of an idol expresses a pretence of reason, ibid. Restoring Dagon to his place: what it means, 137. Dagon, that is, the head of idolatry: what this means, 138. What the palms of his hands signify, ibid. The head and hands of Dagon cut off: what they signify, ibid. Why they were placed on the threshold, ibid. The priests of Dagon imply that they are priests because they do not tread upon the threshold, ibid. The priests of Dagon remain to the present day, ibid.

[Col. 1443]

Damascus is interpreted as “bloody,” 451. The tower of Lebanon looking toward Damascus: what it signifies, ibid. The punishments of eternal condemnation are avoided through the harsh and difficult trials of a very brief time, 274. Condemnation is the second plague of sinners, 308. The blessed do not pity the condemned, 173. The condemned in hell see the blessed in heaven, 89.

Dan signifies the simple. It also signifies the life of sinners, 110. Why Daniel is called “a man of desires,” 333.

David is interpreted as “strong of hand,” 386, 466. David learned that a man does not possess a stable condition of strength in himself, but rather a fall into weakness, 64. What David’s laying aside all military weapons when he was about to fight Goliath signifies, 83. David did not wish to use the royal right of tyrants by accepting the ark from Ornan the Jebusite for a worthy price, 182. Whoever holds the psalter in praise of the Redeemer David, 241. He touched the harp of the Resurrection and Ascension, ibid. David is called a man after God’s heart, 290. David’s good qualities benefited Solomon, 327. What the giving of Michal to David in place of Merab signifies, 335. David is called a triumphant man, 367. His perfection is signified by this name, ibid. David rejected, little, and a shepherd of sheep, 382. Why David is praised as ruddy, ibid. “Beautiful in appearance,” that is, conspicuous through inward contemplation, ibid. David is anointed in the midst of his brothers so that he may benefit all, 385. Christ is foreshadowed in David, 386, 545. What Spirit was directed into David, 392. In David the strength of the holy soul is signified, 466. David is a mirror for penitents, 493. David was holy in tribulation but fell through carelessness in repose, ibid. The seriousness of David’s fall, 495. The incarnation of the Word was foreknown by David, 496. David feared that the promised Christ might be denied him because of his sins, 502. Why David was unable to build a house for the Lord, 509. David is anointed because he will persevere, 386. His devotion toward Saul, 493.

The summary of the Decalogue is enclosed in the numbers one thousand and one hundred, 345. What it means for the king to take a tenth of the flocks, 185. What it means for the produce of fields and vineyards to be tithed, 184, 196. What the tithes demanded each year signify, ibid. How the tithe of good works is to be gathered, 196.

What it means for the ancient enemy to place a snare along the path, 547. To turn aside after vain things is to prefer love of temporal goods to divine love, 276. What it means to turn aside to the right or to the left, 153. “Let him fail from himself” who intends to advance toward God, 551.

The pleasure of sin is signified by the name “salt,” 303. Good works are to be performed from the pleasure of grace, 273. The memory of heavenly conduct opposes the pleasure of sin, 303. The pleasure of lust destroys the virtues, 371. The soul’s delight at the presence of the Bridegroom, 439. What prevents it from enjoying this sweetness for long, ibid. God frees those impeded by the thorns of carnal pleasures, 470. Heavenly delights are to be tasted beforehand in the valley of humility, 155.

How useful it is to remember past offenses, 147. How “to make a known offense” and “to disclose an offense” differ, 476. The number ten signifies the perfection of the ancient Law, 163, 185, 197, 346, 445. The doubled ten is perfected in the conduct of the elect, 163. The perfection of good works is signified by the ten commandments of the Law, 223, 425.

[Col. 1444]

“To knock out the teeth” of those building Babylon is to confound both their deeds and their words, 507. The mighty are cast down from their throne when disobedient and proud men are rejected, 363. How supplication and prayer differ from each other, 539. The Spirit abandons some in time, while taking up others without abandoning them, 386, 392. A man abandoned by God is shaken by the blows of temptations, 487, 492. He is also blinded by darkness, ibid. God abandons the one to whom he does not grant steadfastness in tribulation, 492.

The desert signifies hell, 294. In it no consolation amid sufferings is found, ibid. What the valley of the does facing the desert signifies, ibid. This world is a desert and exile for the holy soul, 455.

Earthly desires are signified by calves, 150. To ask of the soul is to desire; and to rejoice is to sing, 57. What belongs to the soul’s ineffable desire is not expressed in rational speech, 104. Evil desires must be restrained and enclosed so that they do not emerge, 150. As many demons rest in hearts as there are unclean desires, 164. The thunderclaps of the clouds are the fervent desires of the elect, 169. The imperfect desires of Christians are not terrifying to demons, ibid. The chariot of the Church’s leaders consists of their devout desires, 192. We are blackened by earthly desires, 411. How the mind languishing with desire for eternal things may find rest, 417. The desires of the ancient Church awaiting Christ, 454. So that all our desire may be directed toward God, let us despise earthly things and love heavenly things, 486. Delayed desire is turned into punishment, ibid. When carnal desires have been expelled from the heart, the right spirit is renewed, 501. The prophet asks to be freed from “bloods,” that is, carnal desires, 504. Christ is granted to the desires and prayers of the righteous, 525.

One who despairs of the forgiveness of sin sins against the Holy Spirit, 502. Unless God mercifully looks upon us, we fall into despair, 551. To determine something in the heart is to propose it after deliberation, 28.

Why God is called “of hosts,” 12. God is called “the triumphant one,” 366. Why God is sometimes called lord, sometimes father, and sometimes bridegroom, 400. The name “bridegroom” is dearer to God than “father,” and “father” than “lord,” ibid. God is the life of the soul, 470.

What “the face of God” is, 235. What it means for God to answer, 323. God has neither a heart nor a soul, 80. God speaks to a human being as one human being ordinarily speaks to another, ibid. God did not speak to Samuel directly, but through the Evangelical Spirit, 100. “Gods” designate exalted and wise men, 148.

God does not consist of parts belonging to a human being, 80. Heart and soul signify his will, ibid., 290. Human characteristics are attributed to God because of our poverty, 103, 352, 565. The hand of the Lord is the power of divine authority, 138. It is also divine severity, 274. The hand of the Lord is the only-begotten Son of the eternal Father, 152. What it means to speak in God’s ears, 187. The heart of God designates his inmost will, 290. What the right hand or left hand of God signifies, 400.

How one should confess God as his own God in a particular way, 55. We are sanctified by God, led to rest, and glorified, 56. What must be done so that we may serve God alone, 164. It is greater to be joined to God than to be adopted, and greater to be adopted than to be created, 401. Who have God as their rider, 413. The mind’s gaze must be directed toward God, [Col. 1445] 544.
